absent: Semantics of identifier filtering, exception injection and feature test helpers are absent.
Full register descriptor layout and host emulation behavior beyond table routing are absent.
Simple ring buffer mechanics, clock source and lock critical sections beyond the singleton are absent.
Page table level count, granule sizes and entry bit encodings are absent.
Memory operation callbacks for allocation, reference counting and cache maintenance are absent.
Translation invalidation primitives, barrier requirements and deferred flush policy details are absent.
Ownership identifier meanings and annotation update lifecycle are absent.

findings.text: Protected guest handler for AArch64 identifier registers rejects writes by raising an undefined exception and reporting failure, while reads obtain a filtered value from a helper and report success.

Handler for the interrupt controller status register reports a fixed combination of DIB, DFB and SRE enable bits on reads to advertise only version three support and always reports success regardless of access direction.

Handler for selected identification style registers checks a feature field for an implementation defined indicator; when present it raises a synchronous exception using the current syndrome, otherwise it raises an undefined exception, and in both cases reports failure.

Table construction helpers assign a uniform policy per class: AArch32 and AArch64 identifier groups delegate to filtered readers, unallocated identifier encodings reuse the AArch64 reader, debug and error classes reuse a read as zero write ignored policy, and host handled entries leave dispatch empty for host emulation.

Protected guest register table applies restrictive defaults across cache, debug, trace, identifier, vector, error, performance, ordering and activity groups, explicitly lists host emulated cache identifier, interrupt and timer registers, routes unallocated identifier slots to the filtered reader, and routes two cache plus one device identifier to the conditional fault handler.
Public handler for restricted protected guest traps raises an undefined exception for the calling virtual CPU and reports the exit as handled, ignoring the supplied exit code value.
Translation invalidation context bundles a stage two context pointer together with saved control values for translation control and system control.

Hypervisor trace state holds a per CPU ring descriptor pointer, a backing allocation base and length for shared pages, and a hypervisor spin lock; the singleton instance is wired to a per CPU ring store and starts unlocked.
Tracing interface reserves variable length entries from the calling CPU ring with a hypervisor clock timestamp and later commits the most recent reservation on the same CPU.

Shared page setup translates a kernel address to its hypervisor alias and, only when protected mode is active, pins the single page range returning null on failure or unpins on teardown; without protected mode it passes the translated address through and teardown is a no operation.
Page table walk tracking record carries a walker callback reference plus start, current and end address cursors for the range being visited.

Walk helpers report whether break before make invalidation or cache maintenance should be skipped from visit flags, and a block mapping is permitted only when the level supports it, the remaining range covers a full granule, and both physical and virtual addresses align to that granule.

Entry constructors provide clearing to zero, table creation from a child table address with table type and validity, and leaf creation from a physical address with masked low and high attributes plus a page versus block type selected by final level and validity.
Leaf capture callback records the visited entry value and level into a small result record holding an entry plus a level number, and always reports success.
Hypervisor map argument pairs a base physical address with an attribute set to apply across the walked range.

Hypervisor map traversal first attempts a leaf install with physical offsetting and compatibility checks for identical, empty or software only differing entries, otherwise allocates a fresh child table unless at the final level, installs it with a reference increment and ordered store, and propagates allocation or level errors.

Hypervisor unmap traversal requires a present entry, follows tables only when exclusively referenced and leaves shared tables untouched, requires full granule coverage for leaves, clears with a barrier and level appropriate invalidation followed by synchronization, then releases table and child references while counting unmapped bytes for leaves.
Hypervisor free traversal ignores absent entries and otherwise releases the table reference, with an additional child release when the old entry encodes a table, performing no invalidation.

Stage two map argument bundles base physical address, attribute set, annotation entry value, anchor and child pointers, owning context, allocation cache, plus flags forcing page granularity and selecting owner only annotation updates.

Stage two entry predicates treat any invalid to valid transition or any change outside permission bits as needing update, treat any nonzero value as reference counted including foreign ownership encodings, detect a locked state via an invalid type field, and install via plain store when exclusive or compare exchange when shared.

Stage two replacement first marks the slot locked with race detection that warns on unexpected contention in exclusive walks, performs virtual machine scoped invalidation sized by old table or leaf contents unless skipped, releases the old reference when counted, then installs the new value with a counted aware increment and ordered store after asserting the slot is locked.

Stage two teardown helper clears valid entries with immediate invalidation for tables and policy dependent deferred or immediate invalidation for leaves, while cacheability requires validity plus normal memory type and executability derives from the union of user and privileged execute protections.

Stage two leaf attempt derives the physical address from walk progress, enforces page granularity and annotation overrides before block support, skips identical or permission only changes for later relaxation, takes a software only fast path with reference adjustment when exclusive, otherwise breaks the old entry, performs data and instruction maintenance conditioned on skip flags and new entry properties, then installs.

Stage two walk dispatch collapses an existing table to a leaf when allowed and frees the detached table on the pre table visit, splits to a new table from the allocation cache when a leaf is too large on the leaf visit with retry on contention, and rejects any other visit kind.

Stage two unmap traversal clears and releases invalid but counted ownership entries, retains shared tables, evaluates cache clean need from final hardware capability for cacheable leaves, removes whole block entries expecting lazy refill of survivors, and runs post data maintenance plus child release.

Attribute update record holds set and clear masks plus captured entry and level; its walker requires a present entry, merges masks, invalidates instruction cache only when adding new execute permission, tolerates lost access flag races, and signals retry on concurrent install failure.

Aging record holds a clear request and a youth flag; its walker ignores absent entries or already clear access flags, otherwise marks young and optionally clears the flag with retry on contention, leaving invalidation to a core notifier callback.

Trace buffer mutation is serialized by a hypervisor spin lock embedded in the buffer singleton, while stage two aging assumes the caller holds the address space lock for write and other stage two install paths use exclusive stores or shared compare exchange plus a locked entry state to detect races.

Walkers warn and fail on final level table allocation, incompatible leaf replacement, unexpected locked contention, invalid unmap ranges and missing allocation caches, while shared page pinning can return null and concurrent stage two updates signal retry rather than blocking.

Unallocated identifier space fixes the first opcode to three, the second opcode to zero and the N control register to zero while varying the M control register and final opcode, and protected guests observe fixed enable bits for the interrupt controller status register.
